title: Why do cats' eyes shine in the dark?
sources: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine

lines.text: When headlights hit a cat at night, why do their eyes shine like glowing alien headlights?
lines.caps: Why do cats' eyes *glow | in the pitch *dark?

lines.text: Cats possess a biological night-vision mirror behind their retinas called the tapetum lucidum.
lines.caps: They have a mirror *behind | the retina called the *tapetum

lines.text: When light enters a human eye, photoreceptors absorb some and the rest is lost in darkness.
In cats, unabsorbed light strikes this reflective layer of tissue and bounces back through the retina a second time.
lines.caps: Light bounces back through *photoreceptors | a *second time!

lines.text: This double exposure gives felines incredible night vision, letting them hunt in near total blackness.
The eerie glow you see is simply reflected flashlight rays bouncing back out of their eye mirrors.
lines.caps: The glow is *flashlights | bouncing off their eye *mirrors!

lines.text: Nature gave cats built-in night-vision goggles millions of years before humans invented them.
